Confidence Score: 4/5

[Medium impact] The change affects the operator's paged report-history workflow.

Fix the skipped deliveries before merging; adding a supporting index would also prevent slower history pages.

Findings
 Pages skip same-time deliveries ▶
 History lacks a supporting index ▶
Summary

Report history now shows later scheduled deliveries first, with id breaking ties.

Report history lists the latest scheduled deliveries first.

Reviews (1) · Last reviewed commit: "Page report history by scheduled time" · Reviewed by Greptile

Pages skip same-time deliveries. When a page ends among deliveries sharing one scheduled_at, the next cursor contains only that timestamp. The strict < filter then excludes every remaining delivery at that time. For example, three deliveries at the same second with limit=2 return two rows, then an empty page. Shared timestamps are explicitly supported. Keep both scheduled_at and id in the cursor position and compare both when fetching the next page.

Confidence Score: 4/5

[Low impact] The change reaches only the report export workflow.

Restore CSV quoting before merging so exports preserve each delivery.

Findings
 Report names break CSV output ▶
Summary

The PR streams delivery rows from the database into the export instead of loading them all first.

Exports write each delivery as the database returns it.

Reviews (1) · Last reviewed commit: "Stream the report export" · Reviewed by Greptile

Report names break CSV output. Report names accept free-form text, so a name such as Weekly orders, Europe reaches this line unchanged. Joining values with commas writes four fields under a three-column header; embedded newlines can also turn one delivery into several records. Keep csv.writer and writer.writerow(row) while iterating the database cursor. Streaming does not require removing CSV quoting.

Confidence Score: 4/5

[Medium impact] The change affects queue worker runs and the delivery records they update.

Fix the loop bounds before merging so every due job gets processed.

Findings
 Small batches never get delivered ▶
Summary

The PR batches receipt inserts and delivery updates in groups of twenty. It needs one fix before merging: the loop skips every final group smaller than twenty.

The report worker handles due jobs in groups of 20.

Reviews (1) · Last reviewed commit: "Batch queued deliveries" · Reviewed by Greptile

Small batches never get delivered. The loop stops at len(jobs) - batch_size + 1, so it only visits full groups of twenty. With 19 due jobs, deliver_due returns zero without writing anything; with 21, it delivers twenty and leaves one pending. Repeated calls cannot clear the remaining jobs unless more arrive. Use range(0, len(jobs), batch_size) so the final slice is processed too.

Reviews (1) · Last reviewed commit: "Use the new delivery queue" · Reviewed by Greptile

Worker example misses new jobs. The README still tells operators to run work --queue reports. After this change, that command skips newly scheduled jobs because deliver_due matches the queue exactly. Update the example to run report-dispatch, and explain that operators should also drain reports for existing jobs.
